query: What sample sizes, sampling frames, and power calculations are required for plot and household surveys to detect meaningful changes in ESV drivers, and what is the timeline and ethics plan?

response.query: What sample sizes, sampling frames, and power calculations are required for plot and household surveys to detect meaningful changes in ESV drivers, and what is the timeline and ethics plan?
response.answer: To detect meaningful changes in ecosystem service value drivers, sample sizes and power calculations depend on effect size and desired confidence level; typically, larger samples are needed for smaller effect sizes. Ethical considerations include informed consent and data privacy. Timelines vary based on project scope and resources.

results.title: Sample design and estimation for household surveys - ResearchGate
results.content: Published Time: 2002-01-01 (PDF) Sample design and estimation for household surveys Sample design and estimation for household surveys Download full-text PDFRead full-text Household surveys are a widely-used tool for obtaining information about a population of people. Traditional sample design and estimation methods ignore these dependencies.Methodologies which explicitly allow for the dependencies which may arise within households are developed in four areas: Estimating the design effects of standard estimators, for survey design; Constructing new estimators to exploit dependencies within households; Selecting a set of auxiliary variables to use in regression estimation; Allocating the sample sizes of households and of people within households.In each case, new methods will be developed which allow for the population structure of people within households. It is shown that, in estimating the variance at the sample design stage, the variation of household size must be considered. Existing criteria for selecting which auxiliary variables to use in regression estimation are extended to the case of two-stage sampling, and applied to household surveys. The fact that the number of people in a household is small leads to some novel and efficient sample designs and estimators. TWO-STAGE SAMPLE DESIGN WITH SMALL CLUSTERS In two-stage surveys, the sample size of clusters and units within clusters can be chosen to minimise the variance of an estimator, for fixed cost. We develop more flexible designs by optimizing survey cost, based on a simple cost model, subject to a required variance for an estimator of population total. The innovation lies in the fact that household sample sizes are small integers, which creates challenges in both design and estimation. Now is the time to continue hiring in science Discover more about:Household Survey ### On the Relationship of General Designs and Moments of Estimators in Simple Linear Regression Methods are developed for determining sampling designs in simple linear regression (SLR) when residuals are non-normal that permit use of the classical normality-based analyses. Results on design effects for two stage surveys are reviewed and applied to give design effects of household samples. ### Person­ level and household ­level regression estimation in household surveys A common class of survey designs involves selecting all people within selected households.
